page: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dpdsv6 family, powered by 32 dedicated physical cores on a 3.4 GHz ARM Neoverse-N2 processor architecture utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. It offers a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 128 GB of RAM, backed by 128 MB of L3 cache and 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core. Bundled local storage includes a 1890 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance supports Azure Premium Storage options.

The server displays high memory bandwidth performance, recording 448.6 GB/sec read and 188.32 GB/sec write speeds on large data blocks alongside top-tier Passmark memory and database operation scores. Multi-threaded benchmark results place the instance in the top 25% for Geekbench multi-core, stress-ng multi-core CPU testing, software compilation using Clang, and static web serving throughput.

Single-core performance and cryptographic operations remain in the average tier. LLM inference performance drops significantly for large models, placing prompt processing for 70B parameter models in the bottom 10%. The hardware configuration delivers strong qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense workloads such as in-memory caching with Redis, localized relational databases, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and multi-threaded web infrastructure.
description: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine from the Dpdsv6 family based on the 64-bit ARM Neoverse-N2 architecture operating at 3.4 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 32 dedicated physical cores, 128 GB of RAM, 128 MB of L3 cache, and a bundled 1890 GB local NVMe SSD. Hardware performance is highlighted by top-tier memory bandwidth reaching 448.6 GB/sec read and 188.32 GB/sec write speed, alongside top-tier database operation benchmarks. Multi-core performance across Geekbench and stress-ng ranks in the top 25%, while single-core execution remains average. The absence of x86 vector extensions and reduced large-model LLM prompt processing throughput represent key tradeoffs. The resource balance makes it effective for database operations, high-concurrency web serving, Redis caching, and CI/CD compilation workloads requiring efficient local NVMe storage and high memory throughput.
